lines: This temple in India was never built. It was carved, top to bottom, out of one single hill of rock.
More than twelve hundred years ago, carvers looked at a basalt hillside and imagined a temple inside it. The catch? You can't add stone back. Every cut was final.
Step one: cut three deep trenches into the hill, boxing in one giant block of rock.
Step two: start at the very top. They shaped the tower first, then worked their way down, standing on the rock they hadn't removed yet.
Step three: hollow it out. A hall with sixteen pillars, shrines, and a stone bridge, all still part of the hill underneath.
Step four: the details. Elephants carved around the base make it look like they're holding the whole temple up.
And all that waste? An estimated two hundred thousand tonnes of rock, broken off by hand and carried out of the pit.
The result is about thirty meters tall, and it's often called the largest monolith on Earth. One rock. No bricks. No mortar.
